title: IPv6 Routing: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Routing in I P version six does the same job. But the commands are a little different. Let's walk through them.

scenes.heading: Postal service, new codes
scenes.narration: Post offices still keep tables of where to send mail. First, you must switch routing on, with I P version six unicast routing. A static route names a prefix and a next hop. The default route is double colon slash zero. And O S P F version three uses link local addresses to talk.

scenes.heading: OSPFv3 setup
scenes.narration: Setting up O S P F version three takes three lines. First, turn on I P version six routing. Then start O S P F version three. And enable it on each interface.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. The router I D is still thirty two bits. Neighbours use link local addresses. And a link local next hop needs an exit interface.

items.wrong: A link-local next hop needs no interface

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva IPv6 routing lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Turn on I P version six unicast routing first. The default route is double colon slash zero. O S P F version three runs over link local addresses. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva IPv6 routing lab.
